videos.script: Nobody at Carreto asks Renata for an architecture. {{title}} They ask for things: a screen, a report, a feature by the end of the quarter. This lesson is about hearing what sits behind those requests. {{helena}} Helena, the product director, wants shippers to quote and book a truck in one go. She wants it fast, and she wants it always available. {{kinds}} Three kinds of requirement hide in that one sentence: what the system does, how well it has to do it, and what nobody is allowed to change. Business people say the first and assume the second. {{whys}} So Renata asks why, more than once, until the request turns into a goal. Here the goal changes the answer. The slow part is not the screen at all. {{numbers}} Then she asks about consequences until fast becomes a number. Fifteen minutes, for nine requests in ten, and always available becomes a window of hours, with a price on it. {{storm}} You will see a workshop that puts the whole flow on one wall, and finds a process nobody in engineering knew about. {{page}} And at the end, one page that writes it all down, in numbers Helena can check.
